::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Innocents day [28 December 1872]  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels[^1]
:::

My dear [Christabel](people/person_329.qmd)

Thanks for the grand faithful [Gosling](organizations/other_104.qmd) card, which is capital. These two Escorials are all that Goosedom has produced[^2] I never expected any thing of it at Christmas They both seem to be of the childish good kind. No, I have not seen [Garnstone](other_books/otherbook_832.qmd). [Warne](people/person_1433.qmd) is not very liberal of his books. I don’t know what school children would do but for the happy dispensation that makes their own people prefer them to all others! Our mistress is I believe to visit a friend in your parish next week. I can’t say I prefer her to all others! She is quite devoid of the moral influence [her predecessor](people/person_1178.qmd) had

your affectionate
C M Yonge

[Florence Wilford](people/person_1520.qmd)’s [Aunt](people/person_384.qmd) died on Monday-

---

[^1]: The paper has an ornamental decoration: 'Dear Friend Accept This CHRISTMAS Greeting Heart with Heart in Memory Meeting'.
[^2]: The Goslings had been asked to write an essay on ‘The history of the Escorial’, a theme proposed by Pixie (CMY to Mary Fursdon, 15 November 1872)
